issue_context.title: Synology_DSM integration does not allow changing essential configs like the username and password
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The Synology_DSM integration - after it was moved from YAML to UI based (which is good) lost the ability for the user to change essential basic settings like IP address (if I decide to replan the IP range) or password.

After having seen some recent ransomware attacks on various 3rd party boxes I have been changing passwords on several units that are integrated with Home Assistant and I have been a bit shocked to find out that the only way you can change the password in the HA config for Synology_DSM is to delete the entire integration and start all over again.

We need to be able to alter the IP address or domain name, username, and passwords. As a minimum passwords. Changing passwords periodically is part of good safety practice and should not been treated as an exception.

For my Synology I also setup a new user with just the priviledge needed for the integration to work. I got triggered to do all this after seeing how many people lost all their data in a recentl QNAP security incident.

I chose to hack the core.config_entries and then restart Home Assistant. That works just fine. But risky. Users should never have to hack .storage files. The UI should give the same config settings.

For this interation the settings the UI miss are

- Host (IP)
- Port
- Username
- Password

And the existing password should not be displayed. You should just be able to replace it with a new password.

This is a generic issue with many integrations and I will raise reports on several of them

The MQTT integration is a good example of an integration where you can change the original settings

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.5.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Never

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Synology_DSM

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/Synology_DSM

review_comments: This will never happen with the current code. `user_input` is always None, currently.
We normally pass the existing entry data as the `data` parameter instead of in the context, and define a confirm step that is called from the reauth step.
This is unconventional. It would be nice to be able to drop this and just raise `ConfigEntryAuthFailed`.
Why not always do this regardless if reauth or not?
If you come here via discovery, it might have an updated host.
If you can fetch the serial without authentication, you could automatically update the data when it's discovered without requiring any work from the user. Fine with leaving it to a future PR.
